topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture series, and sets out the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Errors and Environmental Influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the origins of cancer by evaluating the balance between intrinsic biological bad luck, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures documented by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens contribute to cancer development, focusing on the synergistic mechanisms of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in causing Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagens, Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of physical, chemical, and promotional carcinogens, including metabolic activation, tissue specificity, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies employed to identify carcinogens and determine their mutagenic potency.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and reflections on balancing risks against benefits in everyday life.
